accuracy.evidence: Every story and sum rechecked: 7 − 3 = 4, 5 + 3 = 8, 4 + 2 = 6, 6 − 2 = 4, 8 − 2 = 6 (Pip's 10 is wrong), 4 + 3 = 7 (Pip right), 5 − 1 = 4 (Pip's 6 wrong), 9 − 1 = 8, 3 + 2 = 5, 3 + 4 = 7, 5 + 2 = 7, 4 − 1 = 3; parameterised items stay within 10 (where a+b<=10; a−b with a ≥ 5, b ≤ 4). The problem types (add to, take from, put together; result and total unknown) match CCSS K.OA.2 and the NC Year 1 one-step problem statement.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early word-problem errors: answering with the change quantity (3 flew away → '3', bird and duck count buttons, tag flew), adding every pair regardless of action (7 birds, 3 fly → 10; tag added), answering 'fewer' in an add-to story (tag tookaway), counting only one part of a put-together set (tag part), wrong order in the number sentence (2 − 6, tag order) and double-counting (tap the same apple again).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstory acts out three different CGI problem structures with their own objects: birds tapped off a fence (take from), ducks dragged from the grass into a pond (add to), apples tapped once each (put together), then a more/fewer story sort, a story-order number sentence from cards, and a dot comparison of Pip's answer against the start. flagtake removes counters, flagaddtog joins mats and flagrepass compares representations; the distinct gate passed under 30% against all labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child does the action first and the operation is named after: the fence visibly has fewer birds and '3' is rejected as 'how many flew away'; the pond fills to 8; the story sort ends with 'More come: add. Some go away: take away.'; the sentence step rejects starting with 2 and rejects + for 'eaten'; Pip's 10 dots are shown longer than the 8 at the start when birds flew away.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with tempting wrong options: 'more birds' after 3 fly away (children who add every pair), and 'fewer than 5' when more ducks come. Each is decided by the task straight after, and the reveal names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating stories with tagged wrong answers: flew ('That is how many moved. Count how many there are at the end.'), added ('Some went away, so there are fewer, not more.'), tookaway, part ('That is only the red apples.'), order ('Start with how many there were at the start: 6.').

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the family kid limit (target 5.0). Canvas and button words are one or two syllables ('Tap a bird to make it fly away.', 'more', 'fewer'); the young class gives 56 px buttons and larger story text. Curriculum terms add, take away, altogether, number sentence, add to / take from / put together are in the adult text.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what a word problem is, a take-from story, an add-to and put-together story, the more-or-fewer question. Adult: standards, problem types and key words; why modelling the action comes first; five named mistakes; what the lab does. No filler pattern, and the 12% overlap gate passed against the taking-away and combining lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light screenshots before and after Show me on every step. Fixed after the first pass: birds flying away left the canvas and covered the story line (they now settle in the sky under the title), and the 0–10 number track in 'Does it make sense?' was too small to read on a phone, so it was replaced by two labelled rows of dots ('Start: 8' vs 'Pip: 10').

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a large button twin: 'Fly away' and answer buttons 3/4/10, 'Swim in' and 8/3/2, 'Count next apple', 'more'/'fewer' labelled with the current story, one button per number-sentence card (minus and plus spelled out in aria-label), and 'makes sense'/'not right'. The canvas aria-label and live region read each message; walk.cjs ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
